quantity.text:
QUANTITY (the TRADE term only). Served return on account a, day t, previous row s:
  ret_t = (V_t - F_t + A_t) / V_s - 1,  V = sum of shares x served close p0, a purchase/sale/reinvestment is internal.

PURCHASE of |q| shares of fund f for cash |c| on effective day t (Trade_Date, next trading day if no bar):
  the table values the new shares at |q| x p0_t(f); valued at what was paid they are worth |c|.
  delta_V_t = |c| - |q| x p0_t ;   delta_ret = delta_V_t / V_s.
  Positive delta_ret = served return too LOW; negative = too high.
  Several funds in one account-day: the delta_V terms are summed, then divided by V_s once.
  A fund with no served close on t: unit is no_close, counted, not computed.

SALE of |q| shares for cash |c| on day t:
  the sold shares are gone from V_t and the cash is in the account, so V_t does not depend on f's close
  on t for the sold shares: nothing on day t is mis-valued by the served close. The sold shares sat in V_s
  at p0_s; that is the CARRIED holding, which this item does NOT revalue. Valuing the sale "at what was
  received" on t therefore changes nothing in V_t: the sale's trade term on day t is ZERO under this definition
  (the symmetric reading, the mis-valuation released that day, |q| x p0_t - |c|, is not in V_t at all, so it is 0 too).
  Sale rows therefore enter the population and the by_kind count, contribute 0 bp, and never enter the over-10bp count by
  themselves. Round 75 found 3 sale days with LOWER returns under the full two-build comparison; there the
  holding at s was revalued (V_s moved), which is the carried-holding term and is outside this quantity.
  A day with a purchase and a sale: the purchase terms are summed and the sale adds 0.

NOT REVALUED: the holding carried from s at the served close (round 75: on ten of twelve purchase days the trade
  term was 75-76 percent of the full change, on two it was all of it).

FLOOR: a change is counted when |delta_ret| > 0.001 (10 basis points) for the headline; |delta_ret| > 0.0001 (1 bp) secondary.

control.rule: agree = |mine - round75| <= max(5 percent of round75, 1 bp)
control.mine: (|c| - |q| x served_close_t) / V_s, |c| and |q| from the custodian row, served close from security_day_price r34, V_s from the r34 served table
control.round75_term: q x (p1_t - p0_t) / V_s, p1 the UNADJUSTED vendor close (round 74 variant build), p0 the served (dividend-adjusted) close; p1 equals the price paid within 1 percent on 12 of 12
control.difference_in_definition: mine uses the price paid (cash / shares) where round 75 uses the unadjusted close p1; shares and V_s are the same in kind (V_s from the r34 table here, from the round 74 baseline build there)

against_round75_pred_minus_pred_h.note: the round 75 record also splits the two-build prediction into a holding-only part Pred_h and a q part Pred - Pred_h (75 to 76 percent of Pred on ten days, all of it on two); that q part is a difference of two builds that nets the holding and the denominator, not the first-order term q x dp / V_s; mine agrees with it on the two all-of-it days only

population.reconciliation: trade_account_days = measured + blank + no_close; with_close = measured + blank; no_close = no unit of the day has a served close

moved_19_vs_other.rule: a day belongs to the group of its largest-contributor fund

on_blank_days_if_measured.rule: V_s = sum of valued account_day_value rows at the account previous row s (literal); strict = every position at s valued (no null value).
on_blank_days_if_measured.reading: Literal V_s sums only the positions that are valued; on a blank (UNPRICED) day most positions are not, so V_s is a partial sum, the ratio is inflated, and the literal count is an upper figure, not a measurement. The strict count (every position at s valued) is the sound one.
on_blank_days_if_measured.validation: on the measured days the account_day_value sum at s equals the table V_s on 31 of 31

headline: 16 of 31 measured trade account-days change by more than 10 basis points when the trade is valued at what was paid (15103 trade account-days in all: 6174 with a served close, 8929 without one); bands 10-50: 9, 50-200: 5, over 200: 2. This is the TRADE term only: the carried holding is not revalued, and a sale contributes nothing to V on its day. The 6143 blank trade account-days are counted apart and are not added.
not_established: Only 31 of 15103 trade account-days are measured: 8929 have no served close for any traded fund and 6143 fall on a blank day (almost all UNPRICED). The count says nothing about the other 15072 account-days, nor about the funds outside the 270 series (no served close) whose trades are not in the population.

The change counted is the first-order trade term (|c| - |q| x close_t) / V_s on the served table; it is not a rebuilt return: no chain was run, and the carried holding at the served close (and V_s itself) is not revalued, so the full change on a trade day can differ (round 75: on ten of twelve purchase days the q part was 75 to 76 percent of the two-build prediction).

A sale day contributes zero by definition: the sold shares leave V_t. Whether the mis-valued carried holding in V_s moves the return on sale days (round 75 found 3 sale days with LOWER returns in the two-build comparison) or on the following days is not measured here.

Price paid is amount over quantity from the custodian and includes any sales charge or fee in the amount; a 1 to 5 percent gap can be a load and not a wrong close. The price-fit bands tell fee-sized gaps from large ones; they do not prove which close is right.
Multi-fund days sum the unit terms and take the price-fit band from the largest contributor; 0 measured days carry a unit with no close (not computed), which would make that day a lower bound.

The blank-day count is over a partial V_s on most days (literal rule) and is an upper figure; the strict count covers only blank days whose previous row has every position valued. Neither was added to the headline.
The 31 measured days sit in 13 accounts and 9 funds: the measured set is what the served table prices, not a sample of the 377 holders.
